findings.title: A genuine quoted request containing a document term loses its attribution advisory
findings.observed: Both speech-cue expressions enumerate said/says/replied/responded/answered/wrote/message/words/told/stated. The later documentTerm expression exempts the entire candidate whenever it contains a quoted field/term/etc. The new fixture covers replied and a document-term-only requested sentence, but no mixed request.
findings.staticCase: The operator requested: “Rename the field 'status' to 'state'.”
findings.reason: By static inspection this remains an operator-word candidate, but neither speech-cue expression recognizes requested; the inner field quote matches documentTerm, so the new classification is document-term and the CLI emits NOTE instead of the prior ADVISORY. This is an actual quoted operator instruction, not an incidental document-token-only record. The control therefore does not cover the mixed shape despite step 23 requiring attributed speech to remain distinguished from incidental quotes.
findings.certainty: Statically inferred from the supplied hunk; no probe or test was run by this worker.
findings.remedy: Keep uncertain/mixed attributed records in attributed-speech. Constrain the document-term exemption to the incidental quote occurrence rather than exempting a whole record merely because it contains one, and add a docs-check-fixtures case for the quoted requested instruction (plus a mixed speech/document-term case). Preserve historical keys/fingerprints and the advisory/typed-refusal boundary.
